s.g: Decorated with an attribute.
The act of attributing something.
An explicit or formal acknowledgment of ownership or authorship.
ex: The attribution of the quote is widely regarded as dubious.

s.g: A legal doctrine by which liability is extended to a defendant who did not actually commit the tortious or criminal act.
An adjective that modifies the head of the noun phrase in which it occurs; an adjective that precedes the word or phrase it modifies.
ex: The word “red” in “the red balloon” is an attributive adjective.
In the phrase “attributive adjective”, “attributive” is the attributive adjective.

s.g: Grinding down or wearing away by friction.
The wearing of teeth due to their grinding.
A gradual reduction in number.
A gradual, natural reduction in membership or personnel, as through injury, incapacitation, retirement, resignation, or death.
To grind or wear down through friction.
ex: attritioned teeth; attritioned rock

s.g: To reduce the number of (jobs or workers) by not hiring new employees to fill positions that become vacant (often with out).
To undergo a reduction in number.
ex: The cohort of one hundred students had attritioned to sixty by the end of secondary school.

s.g: Tuned to the correct pitch.
Brought into harmony; harmonized.
Having been changed to fit in with a particular context or to be in sync with a phenomenon.
